# Error codes

Every problem ship reports carries a stable code: `SHIP-E` for errors, `SHIP-W` for warnings, `SHIP-I` for information. Codes are never reused, so you can search for one. The messages below are the ones ship prints, with `{placeholders}` for the values it fills in; most of them say what to do. `ship doctor` finds the most common problems before they stop you, and `ship fix` repairs several of them.

Exit codes: `0` success, `1` error, `2` a person must act, `3` a safety check refused the work, `5` refused by the organisation policy, `64` wrong usage, `130` cancelled.

## General

### SHIP-E0001

*Exit code 1.*

> Unexpected error: {error}

## Environment, checked by ship doctor

### SHIP-E0301

*Exit code 1.*

> git is not installed.

To fix it: xcode-select --install · sudo apt install git · winget install Git.Git

### SHIP-E0302

*Exit code 1.*

> git {version} is too old; ship-it needs {minimum} or newer.

To fix it: brew install git · Install a newer git from your distribution or git-scm.com · winget upgrade Git.Git

### SHIP-E0303

*Exit code 1.*

> git does not know who you are (user.name / user.email).

To fix it: ship fix (uses your GitHub name and private noreply address), or git config --global user.name "Your Name" and user.email

`ship fix` can do it: Set your git identity (global): {name} <{email}>, GitHub's private address that keeps your e-mail out of the history.

### SHIP-W0304

*Warning: ship goes on.*

> Paths longer than 260 characters are refused (core.longpaths).

To fix it: git config --global core.longpaths true

`ship fix` can do it: Accept paths longer than 260 characters in this repository (core.longpaths).

### SHIP-W0305

*Warning: ship goes on.*

> Not inside a git repository: there is no .github/ship.json here. Use --user for your user file.

> Not inside a git repository.

To fix it: git init

### SHIP-E0306

*Exit code 1.*

> A {operation} is in progress and must be finished first.

### SHIP-W0307

*Warning: ship goes on.*

> HEAD is detached: work is not on a branch.

To fix it: git switch -c <branch> (ship does it for you when you ship)

### SHIP-W0308

*Warning: ship goes on.*

> No "{remote}" remote: ship-it cannot publish yet.

To fix it: git remote add {remote} <url>

### SHIP-W0309

*Warning: ship goes on.*

> Remote "{remote}" mirrors every ref: a push would also send local checkpoints.

To fix it: git config --unset remote.{remote}.mirror

`ship fix` can do it: Stop mirroring remote {remote}: a git push --mirror would also send ship-it's local data.

### SHIP-W0310

*Warning: ship goes on.*

> No GitHub token for {host}: ship can commit, not publish.

To fix it: gh auth login --hostname {host} (or set GH_TOKEN)

### SHIP-W0311

*Warning: ship goes on.*

> GitHub refuses the token from {source} (expired, revoked or SSO not authorized).

To fix it: gh auth refresh --hostname {host} (or a new token, authorized for SSO)

### SHIP-W0312

*Warning: ship goes on.*

> The token from {source} does not see {repository}.

To fix it: git remote get-url origin (check owner and name, and the token's repository access)

### SHIP-W0313

*Warning: ship goes on.*

> GitHub ({host}) does not answer.

To fix it: https://www.githubstatus.com and your proxy (HTTPS_PROXY); local work goes on

### SHIP-W0314

*Warning: ship goes on.*

`ship fix` can do it: Stop tracking {count} files that must never be committed (kept on disk), and ignore {patterns}.

### SHIP-W0315

The remote is not a GitHub repository; local work only.

*Warning: ship goes on.*

> Remote "{remote}" is not a GitHub repository: ship can commit, not publish.

To fix it: ship --local commits without publishing; to publish, point {remote} to GitHub: git remote set-url {remote} <url>

### SHIP-E0316

A command that works on a repository ran outside one.

*Exit code 1.*

> Not inside a git repository: cd into your project, or run git init.

> Not inside a git repository: {command} removes a repository's data from inside it. Your own files go with ship uninstall --user.

### SHIP-E0317

The classic token lacks the scope every push and pull request needs (repo, or public_repo for a public repository).

*Exit code 1.*

> The token lacks the {scope} scope: GitHub will refuse every push and pull request.

To fix it: gh auth refresh --hostname {host} --scopes {scope} (or a token with the {scope} scope in GH_TOKEN)

### SHIP-W0318

The classic token lacks a scope this repository will need: workflow to push workflow files, project for the roadmap.

*Warning: ship goes on.*

> The token lacks the project scope, and github.project.url is set: ship roadmap sync cannot update the project.

> The token lacks the workflow scope, and this branch changes .github/workflows: GitHub will refuse the push.

To fix it: gh auth refresh --hostname {host} --scopes {scope} (or a token with the {scope} scope in GH_TOKEN)

### SHIP-W0319

Ship doctor --deep could not run one of its checks.

*Warning: ship goes on.*

> Project checks not run: they could not start.

> Rulesets not checked: GitHub could not be asked, or HEAD is detached.

> Token scopes not checked: GitHub could not be asked.

To fix it: https://www.githubstatus.com and your proxy (HTTPS_PROXY); local work goes on · ship check gates (shows why)

### SHIP-E0401

*Exit code 1.*

### SHIP-E0402

*Exit code 1.*

### SHIP-E0404

*Exit code 2: a person must act.*

> The repository moved since that delivery (on {branch}, now on {current}); undoing would lose work, so nothing changed.

### SHIP-E0405

*Exit code 2: a person must act.*

### SHIP-E0406

*Exit code 1.*

### SHIP-E0407

*Exit code 2: a person must act.*

> Undoing this publication changes GitHub: it closes pull request #{number} and deletes the remote branch {branch}. Run ship undo in a terminal, or ship undo --yes.

> Undoing this publication changes GitHub: it closes pull request #{number}, deletes the remote branch {branch} and puts back what it changed on issue #{issue} (its status in the project, the assignee it added). Run ship undo in a terminal, or ship undo --yes.

> Undoing this roadmap sync changes GitHub: {issues} created issues closed as not planned, {milestones} created milestones deleted when empty, {items} items removed from the project, states, project fields and sub-issue links put back. Run ship undo --yes to confirm.

> Undoing this stack changes GitHub: it closes the {count} pull requests that are not merged, dissolves the stack and deletes their remote branches ({branch} to {top}). Run ship undo in a terminal, or ship undo --yes.

> Undoing this sync changes GitHub: it puts back the remote branches it pushed or deleted ({branches}) where nobody pushed since, and undoes its {pull_requests} pull request changes. Run ship undo in a terminal, or ship undo --yes.

### SHIP-E0408

*Exit code 1.*

> This work is merged ({url}): a merge cannot be undone; revert it with a new pull request.

### SHIP-E0409

*Exit code 1.*

> Someone pushed to {branch} since: the remote branch is kept, nothing of theirs is lost.

### SHIP-E0410

A configuration file changed since ship-it read it (ship config set, ship undo of an edit); nothing was written.

*Exit code 2: a person must act.*

> {file} changed while ship-it was editing it: nothing was written. Run the command again.

> {file} changed since {key} was edited: ship undo keeps that later change, nothing changed. Edit the file, or use ship config set or unset.

### SHIP-W0411

Undoing a publication found the linked issue's status in the project changed since; ship undo keeps that change.

*Warning: ship goes on.*

> The status of issue #{issue} in the project {project} changed since the publication: ship undo keeps that change.

### SHIP-W0610

*Warning: ship goes on.*

> {branch} conflicts with {base}: published as it is, the pull request will show the conflict. To resolve it: git rebase {base}, fix the files, git rebase --continue, then ship publish.

### SHIP-W0611

### SHIP-E0612

A ruleset's branch name pattern rejects the branch and ship-it may not or cannot rename it.

*Exit code 1.*

> A ruleset of this repository refuses the branch name {branch} (rule "{rule}": the name {requirement}), and no name derived from it fits. Nothing was pushed. Rename it yourself: git branch -m {branch} <new-name>, then ship publish.

> A ruleset of this repository refuses the branch name {branch} (rule "{rule}": the name {requirement}), and ship-it renames only the branches it created and never pushed. Nothing was pushed. Rename it: {command}, then ship publish.

### SHIP-E0613

A commit of the branch breaks a ruleset's commit message pattern.

*Exit code 1.*

> Commit {commit} ({subject}) breaks a ruleset of this repository (rule "{rule}": the message {requirement}). Nothing was pushed, and ship-it never rewrites your history: reword it (git commit --amend for the last commit, git rebase -i {base} otherwise), then ship publish.

### SHIP-E0614

A commit's author or committer e-mail breaks a ruleset's e-mail pattern.

*Exit code 1.*

> Commit {commit} is authored by {email}, which a ruleset of this repository refuses (rule "{rule}": the address {requirement}). Nothing was pushed. Set the right address (git config user.email), redo the authorship (git commit --amend --reset-author --no-edit for the last commit, git rebase -i {base} otherwise), then ship publish.

> Commit {commit} was committed by {email}, which a ruleset of this repository refuses (rule "{rule}": the address {requirement}). Nothing was pushed. Set the right address (git config user.email), recommit (git commit --amend --no-edit for the last commit, git rebase -i {base} otherwise), then ship publish.

### SHIP-E0615

A ruleset requires signed commits and one is not.

*Exit code 1.*

> Commit {commit} ({subject}) is not signed, and a ruleset of this repository requires signed commits. Nothing was pushed. Set up signing (with SSH: git config gpg.format ssh, git config user.signingkey <public key file>, git config commit.gpgsign true), sign the branch's commits (git rebase --exec "git commit --amend --no-edit -S" {base}), then ship publish.

### SHIP-W0616

Ship-it renamed its own branch for a ruleset.

*Warning: ship goes on.*

> Renamed {from} to {to}: a ruleset of this repository requires it (rule "{rule}": the name {requirement}). ship undo gives the old name back.

### SHIP-W0617

Merging the base into the branch (ship.publish.update merge) conflicts; the branch is published as it is.

*Warning: ship goes on.*

> {branch} conflicts with {base}: published as it is, the pull request will show the conflict. To resolve it: git merge {base}, fix the files, git commit, then ship publish.

### SHIP-E0618

A request to GitHub got no answer (network, proxy, outage).

*Exit code 1.*

> GitHub ({host}) does not answer: see https://www.githubstatus.com and your proxy (HTTPS_PROXY).

### SHIP-W0619

An open pull request changes the same or adjacent lines as the branch, a likely conflict for whoever merges second; the publication goes on.

*Warning: ship goes on.*

> Open pull request #{number} ({title}) changes the same lines in {files}: a conflict is likely for whoever merges second. {url}

### SHIP-E0901

*Exit code 3: a safety check refused the work.*

> {count} secrets in your changes: nothing was committed. Move each value to an ignored file (.env.local) or an environment variable; a false positive: add the fingerprint shown to ship.secrets.allow, or its file to ship.secrets.ignorePaths.

> {count} secrets in commits not pushed yet: nothing was pushed. Remove them from the history first (git rebase -i {base}, then edit those commits), and revoke the secret if it is real.

### SHIP-E0902

*Exit code 3: a safety check refused the work.*

> {gate} is red ({command}): nothing was pushed, your commit stays local. Fix it, then ship publish.

> {gate} is red ({command}): nothing was committed. Fix it, then run ship check gates again.

> {gate} is red ({command}): nothing was committed. Fix it, then run ship again.

### SHIP-E0903

*Exit code 3: a safety check refused the work.*

> {tool} is not installed and the {gate} gate needs it: npm install -g {tool}, then ship publish.

> {tool} is not installed and the {gate} gate needs it: nothing was committed. npm install -g {tool}, then run ship check gates again.

> {tool} is not installed and the {gate} gate needs it: nothing was committed. npm install -g {tool}, then run ship again.

### SHIP-E0904

--skip-gates while ship.gates.allowSkip is false.

*Exit code 3: a safety check refused the work.*

### SHIP-E0905

The project's commitlint rejects the message.

### SHIP-E0906

> The project's commitlint does not allow the type {type} (allowed: {allowed}), and no single allowed type means the same: nothing was committed. Pick one, then ship again.

## Stacks of pull requests

### SHIP-E1001

The work cannot make a stack of at least two layers (a single area, an empty layer).

*Exit code 1.*

> The layer {layer} holds no changed file.

> The work touches a single area: there is nothing to stack. Run ship for one pull request, or choose the layers with --layer.

> A stack needs at least two layers ({count} given).

### SHIP-E1002

The current branch is not a layer of a stack ship-it built.

*Exit code 1.*

> {branch} is not a layer of a stack ship-it built. Run ship stack from the default branch to make one.

### SHIP-E1003

GitHub refused to create or change the stack (422: the pull requests cannot form one; 409: another request is changing it).

*Exit code 1.*

> The pull request of {parent} is not open: the new layer is not in a stack.

> GitHub did not group the pull requests in a stack ({detail}); they stay open as a chain.

### SHIP-E1004

The stack is published from its top layer only, where every layer's commits are reachable.

*Exit code 1.*

> You are on {branch}: publish the stack from its top layer, {top}.

### SHIP-E1005

A new layer sits on a layer that is not on GitHub yet; its pull request would have no base.

*Exit code 1.*

> {branch} is based on {parent}, which is not on GitHub yet: publish the stack first (ship stack publish).

### SHIP-E1006

Ship stack merge needs a human's confirmation in a terminal, or --yes; never an AI agent.

*Exit code 2: a person must act.*

> Merging a stack is a human's decision: run ship stack merge in a terminal and confirm, or add --yes. An agent never merges.

### SHIP-E1007

GitHub ran the merge and it failed (a rule, a check, a conflict); nothing was merged.

*Exit code 1.*

> GitHub did not merge #{number}: {detail}. Nothing was merged.

### SHIP-W1008

The merge did not finish while ship-it waited; it goes on on GitHub.

*Warning: ship goes on.*

> GitHub is still merging; follow it on {url}, then run ship stack sync.

### SHIP-W1009

The stack joined the merge queue, which merges it later.

*Warning: ship goes on.*

> The stack is in the merge queue: GitHub merges it once the checks pass ({url}).

### SHIP-W1010

With ship.stack.rebase = github, a layer holds commits that were never pushed; its branch is left alone.

*Warning: ship goes on.*

> {branch} holds commits that were never pushed: it was left as it is. Push it, or set ship.stack.rebase to local.

### SHIP-W1011

Rebasing a layer on the one below conflicted; the rebase was aborted and that layer and those above are left as they were.

*Warning: ship goes on.*

> Rebasing {branch} on {onto} conflicts: it was left as it was, with the layers above. Resolve it with git rebase, then run ship stack sync again.

### SHIP-W1012

No layer of the stack was merged.

*Warning: ship goes on.*

> No layer of the stack is merged: nothing to sync.

### SHIP-E1013

Ship stack starts from the default branch, where the bottom layer is based.

*Exit code 1.*

> You are on {branch}: ship stack starts from the default branch, where the bottom layer is based. On the top layer of a stack, ship adds a layer.

### SHIP-E1014

A sync rebases and switches branches; the work in progress must be committed (or put aside) first.

*Exit code 1.*

> ship stack sync rebases and switches branches: commit or put aside your changes first.

### SHIP-W1015

Undoing a stack sync found a remote branch, the base of a pull request or its chain line changed by someone since; theirs is kept, the rest of the undo goes on.

*Warning: ship goes on.*

> Pull request #{number} targets {base}, changed since the sync: it is kept.

> The chain line of pull request #{number} was edited since the sync: it is kept.

> Someone pushed to {branch} since the sync: their commits stay on GitHub, the layer is back here only ({detail}).
